questions.stem: In India, 'headline inflation' is most commonly and officially measured for monetary policy purposes using which economic index?
questions.explanation: Since 2014, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officially adopted the Consumer Price Index (CPI - Combined) as the key measure of headline inflation to guide its monetary policy and interest rate decisions.

questions.stem: What exactly does the economic acronym 'WPI' stand for in the context of the Indian economy?
questions.explanation: WPI stands for Wholesale Price Index. It measures the changes in the prices of goods sold and traded in bulk by wholesale businesses to other businesses, rather than to everyday consumers.

questions.stem: Which official government organization in India is primarily responsible for compiling and publishing the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
questions.explanation: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is compiled and published monthly by the National Statistical Office (NSO), which operates under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

questions.stem: In the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) basket of India, which specific broad category of goods currently carries the highest overall weightage?
questions.explanation: The WPI basket is divided into three main groups. Manufactured Products carry the highest weight (over 64%). Primary Articles (like food and non-food agricultural items) carry about 22%, and Fuel & Power carry about 13%. (Services are NOT included in WPI).

questions.stem: Which specific mathematical economic formula for constructing a price index number strictly uses 'base year quantities' as its primary weights?
questions.explanation: The Laspeyres Price Index uses the quantities consumed in the base year as fixed weights (Formula: ΣP1Q0 / ΣP0Q0). The Paasche Index, on the other hand, uses current year quantities as weights (ΣP1Q1 / ΣP0Q1).
